narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story of Jonas briskly, including every speech introduction and aside.

jonas.name: Jonas
jonas.note: The reluctant prophet, son of Amathi; resigned in the storm, fervent in prayer, sullen and angry at Ninive's pardon.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God speaking to his prophet; commanding, then patient and gently questioning.

1.t: And Jonah was exceedingly troubled, and was angry:

2.t: And he prayed to the Lord, and said:

I beseech thee, O Lord, is not this what I said, when I was yet in my own country? therefore I went before to flee into Tharsis: for I know that thou art a gracious and merciful God, patient, and of much compassion, and easy to forgive evil.

3.t: And now, O Lord, I beseech thee take my life from me: for it is better for me to die than to live.

4.t: Dost thou think thou hast reason to be angry?

5.t: Then Jonah went out of the city, and sat toward the east side of the city: and he made himself a booth there, and he sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would befall the city.

6.t: And the Lord God prepared an ivy, and it came up over the head of Jonah, to be a shadow over his head, and to cover him (for he was fatigued): and Jonah was exceeding glad of the ivy.

7.t: But God prepared a worm, when the morning arose on the following day: and it struck the ivy and it withered.

8.t: And when the sun was risen, the Lord commanded a hot and burning wind: and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, and he broiled with the heat: and he desired for his soul that he might die, and said:
It is better for me to die than to live.

9.t: And the Lord said to Jonah:
Dost thou think thou hast reason to be angry, for the ivy?
I am angry with reason even unto death.

10.t: Thou art grieved for the ivy, for which thou hast not laboured, nor made it to grow, which in one night came up, and in one night perished.

11.t: And shall I not spare Ninive, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons, that know not how to distinguish between their right hand and their left, and many beasts?
